tEn: Paper: An AI-Native Design Tool for the Next Era
tZh: Paper：面向下一个时代的 AI 原生设计工具
sEn: Steven Haney, founder of Paper, discusses how his AI-native design tool leverages HTML and CSS to empower designers and agents alike.
sZh: Paper 创始人 Steven Haney 探讨其 AI 原生设计工具如何利用 HTML 和 CSS 赋能设计师与智能体。

consensus.en: Design is a key differentiator; great companies of the last 10-20 years all have exceptional design.
consensus.zh: 设计是关键差异化因素；过去10-20年的伟大公司都拥有卓越的设计。

consensus.en: Using HTML and CSS as the rendering engine makes it easier for agents to work with design tools.
consensus.zh: 使用HTML和CSS作为渲染引擎使智能体更容易与设计工具协作。

consensus.en: The codebase should be the single source of truth for design and development, eliminating the need for separate design systems.
consensus.zh: 代码库应作为设计和开发的唯一事实来源，无需维护两套设计系统。

consensus.en: Agents can speed up design work, but human oversight and curation are essential for quality and uniqueness.
consensus.zh: 智能体可以加速设计工作，但人类的监督和策展对于质量和独特性至关重要。

consensus.en: Talking to users daily and staying values-aligned with the market are crucial for building a successful product.
consensus.zh: 每天与用户交流并保持与市场价值观一致对于构建成功产品至关重要。

contrarian.en: AI-generated designs often have telltale signs like overuse of bold fonts, too many font sizes, and generic gradients.
contrarian.zh: AI生成的设计常有明显特征，如过度使用粗体、字体大小过多、通用渐变等。

contrarian.en: Designers should avoid using whatever AI spits out; it makes them look like one of a million other projects.
contrarian.zh: 设计师应避免直接使用AI生成的内容；这会让作品看起来像百万个项目中的一个。

contrarian.en: Agents will never replace human design decision-making because design involves organizational dynamics and stakeholder management.
contrarian.zh: 智能体永远不会取代人类的设计决策，因为设计涉及组织动态和利益相关者管理。

contrarian.en: Even at a fast-moving AI-native company, we still read every line of code and avoid agents in core product development.
contrarian.zh: 即使在快速发展的AI原生公司，我们仍然逐行阅读代码，并在核心产品开发中避免使用智能体。

contrarian.en: Vibe-coded sites often include light/dark mode toggles, which are rarely necessary and are a tell of AI generation.
contrarian.zh: Vibe编码的网站通常包含浅色/深色模式切换，这很少必要，是AI生成的标志。

turns.en: The agents can speed you up. They can save you a lot of work, and they can do tasks like translation or resizing for you. But we're big believers in the human element of design and how important that is. And so, we're trying to create a tool that lets humans work really fast with agents. It's probably very tempting to use whatever Cloud Design spits out. I don't think it helps you stand out from the crowd. And so, I think design is this great differentiator. And if you look at every great company of the last 10 or 20 years, basically all of them have exceptional design. And so, I think if you want to be one of those really great companies, you have to put the care in on design and make sure that you stand out.
turns.zh: 智能体可以帮你提速，帮你省下大量工作，还能替你完成翻译、调整尺寸之类的任务。但我们坚信设计中人的因素至关重要。所以，我们想打造一个让人类能与智能体高效协作的工具。直接照搬 Cloud Design 生成的结果确实很诱人，但我觉得那并不能让你脱颖而出。我认为设计是巨大的差异化优势。看看过去一二十年的每一家伟大公司，基本上都拥有卓越的设计。所以，如果你想成为那样伟大的公司，就必须在设计上倾注心血，确保自己与众不同。

turns.en: Today, I'm excited to welcome Steven Haney, the founder of Paper, an AI-native design tool that's been taking the design world by storm. We're already using Paper a ton here at YC for all of the design work that we're doing internally, and I'm excited for him to show off how the product works to everybody out there. So, Steven, thank you so much for joining.
turns.zh: 今天，我很高兴邀请到 Paper 的创始人 Steven Haney。Paper 是一款 AI 原生的设计工具，正在设计界掀起风暴。我们在 YC 内部已经大量使用 Paper 来处理所有设计工作。我很期待他能向各位展示这款产品的运作方式。Steven，非常感谢你的到来。

turns.en: Yeah, I'm honored to be here. I've watched the show a lot, and so, it's really, really nice to be on. Thank you for having me.
turns.zh: 是的，我很荣幸能来到这里。我经常看这个节目，所以能上节目真的非常开心。感谢你的邀请。

turns.en: Maybe to start, tell people what is Paper.
turns.zh: 也许先开始，给大家介绍一下 Paper 是什么吧。

turns.en: Yeah, well, Paper is a design tool. It's an agent-native design tool. And what that means is we use HTML and CSS as the actual rendering engine, and that makes it very easy for agents to use because they understand HTML and CSS really well. And historically, a lot of design tools have custom rendering engines, and those are a lot harder for agents to use. And so, you'll see higher token spend, slower times, lower accuracy. So, what we're building with Paper is basically a group of people. It's about 12 of us now. All designers and engineers. We basically started this out of love for design, and now we're just trying to build the best design tool possible for this next era.
turns.zh: 是的，Paper 是一款设计工具，是一款智能体原生的设计工具。这意味着我们使用 HTML 和 CSS 作为实际的渲染引擎，这让智能体非常容易上手，因为它们对 HTML 和 CSS 理解得很好。而历史上很多设计工具都使用自定义渲染引擎，那些对智能体来说就难得多，你会看到更高的 token 消耗、更慢的速度、更低的准确性。所以，我们用 Paper 打造的是一个团队，现在大约 12 人，全是设计师和工程师。我们基本上是出于对设计的热爱而创办了这家公司，现在只是努力为这个新时代打造最好的设计工具。

turns.en: Yeah, it's crazy to think you're only 12 people because I hear about you all the time from everybody who's using you, and especially from so many founders that are just picking the design tool that they want to build and live in all of the time, and doing that from the ground floor being AI-native themselves. They're looking for the AI-native tool that is going to work best.
turns.zh: 是啊，很难想象你们只有 12 个人，因为我经常从所有使用你们产品的人那里听到你们，尤其是很多创始人，他们正在挑选自己想要构建并一直使用的设计工具，而且他们自己从一开始就是 AI 原生的，他们正在寻找最适合自己的 AI 原生工具。

turns.en: Absolutely.
turns.zh: 完全正确。

turns.en: So, maybe talk about what was your inspiration for building Paper, and why were some of the existing tools that are out there not good enough for you?
turns.zh: 那么，也许谈谈你构建 Paper 的灵感是什么，为什么现有的那些工具对你来说不够好？

turns.en: It really was born from a love of design. As I said, I started as a solo founder, and it was really the side project that just kind of kept going. I had months where I was like, is anyone going to care about Paper? And then it was like, oh yeah, people do care, you know, this is great, it's really taking off. It was the thing I was going to do anyway. It was very much the thing I was going to do anyway, which I really believe starting a startup you should do that. You should do the thing you're going to do anyway, you should do the thing where you have founder market fit. And for me, this is where I had the strongest founder market fit, because I love building tools for creative professionals. It's something I'm going to wake up every day, and like I'm not going to have a bad day building creative tooling. So, that came first, even before the market or competitors or any of that kind of thing. And then looking around, it was like, well gosh, I mean, you know, we're big fans of Figma, you almost can't talk about design without saying, you know, Figma these days. They've done a lot for the design industry. They have a huge company now, and they're doing very well with enterprise companies. And we were thinking, well, maybe there's time for a new tool to focus on the designer, and just really spend a lot of time. There's so much change with AI agents. Can we build something that's agent native, building on HTML and CSS, and just build this, you know, next gen tool? And so, that's kind of what we're going after, and so far so good.
turns.zh: 这确实源于对设计的热爱。正如我所说，我是以独立创始人的身份起步的，这其实是一个一直持续下去的副业项目。有几个月我都在想，会有人在意 Paper 吗？然后发现，哦，是的，人们确实在意，你知道，这太棒了，它真的起飞了。这是我无论如何都会去做的事情。这确实是我无论如何都会去做的事情，我坚信创业就应该这样。你应该去做你本来就会做的事情，你应该去做你拥有创始人市场契合度的事情。对我来说，这就是我创始人市场契合度最强的地方，因为我喜欢为创意专业人士构建工具。这是我每天醒来都会去做的事情，而且我构建创意工具时不会有糟糕的一天。所以，这优先于市场或竞争对手等一切。然后环顾四周，我想，天哪，你知道，我们是 Figma 的忠实粉丝，如今谈论设计几乎不可能不提 Figma。他们为设计行业做出了巨大贡献。他们现在是一家大公司，在企业客户方面做得很好。我们在想，也许现在是时候出现一款专注于设计师的新工具了，并且真正投入大量时间。AI 智能体带来了如此多的变化。我们能否构建一个智能体原生的、基于 HTML 和 CSS 的工具，打造出下一代工具呢？这就是我们的目标，到目前为止一切顺利。

turns.en: Yeah, and what does that mean to be an AI-native, agent-native design tool?
turns.zh: 是的，那么作为一款 AI 原生、智能体原生的设计工具，这意味着什么？

turns.en: It's really about the fundamental technology. So, using HTML and CSS as the rendering engine, we actually did it to help with designer-developer handoff. We were like, hey, if the designer can have this constraint-free system where it feels like a Figma or a Sketch, but by the way, it's HTML. They don't have to know that. That's great, the handoff will be better. It turns out, if you build a great handoff for humans, you've also built a great handoff for agents, because agents understand HTML and CSS, and it's in their training data. And so, when you ask an agent to work with a Paper file, it's literally just reading the CSS out. And agents know exactly what to do with it. You try to basically extend the agent with a visual interface. It's sometimes that I get it paper is a design tool, but it's also this visual interface for agents. We see sales folks, engineers, all kinds of people are using it because prompting isn't always the best input mechanism for agents. Sometimes you want to drag and draw and it's just faster to be able to do direct manipulation.
turns.zh: 这实际上关乎底层技术。所以，使用 HTML 和 CSS 作为渲染引擎，我们这样做是为了帮助设计师与开发者的交接。我们想，嘿，如果设计师能拥有一个无约束的系统，感觉像 Figma 或 Sketch，但顺便说一句，它是 HTML。他们不必知道这一点。那太好了，交接会更好。事实证明，如果你为人类构建了出色的交接，你也为智能体构建了出色的交接，因为智能体理解 HTML 和 CSS，这些都在它们的训练数据中。所以，当你让智能体处理 Paper 文件时，它实际上只是读取 CSS。智能体完全知道该怎么处理。你基本上是在尝试用可视化界面扩展智能体。有时候我理解 Paper 是一款设计工具，但它也是智能体的可视化界面。我们看到销售、工程师等各类人都在使用它，因为提示并不总是智能体的最佳输入机制。有时你想拖拽和绘制，直接操作会更快。

turns.en: Yeah, it's interesting because as it becomes easier and easier to build software, the figuring out what to build and getting inspiration for how to build it seems to be one of the trickiest pieces right now and one of the biggest bottlenecks. How do you think about using Paper to be able to solve that piece of the creative workflow?
turns.zh: 是的，这很有趣，因为随着构建软件变得越来越容易，弄清楚要构建什么以及如何获得构建灵感似乎成了目前最棘手的问题之一，也是最大的瓶颈之一。你认为如何使用 Paper 来解决创意工作流程中的这一部分？

turns.en: We see there's more software than ever being created and engineering teams are moving so fast now. And I don't know how you feel about this, but I haven't felt like the software is getting better necessarily. I haven't had a great software experience in the last 6 months that blew me away. And so it's important for us, like I grew up as a fan of software. I love building great software. The best compliment you can give me is that Paper is really great software. And so I want more of that for the world, and so I want to help designers and people with taste keep up, you know, with all of the software that's being created. And so giving them a tool that can move at the speed of prompting and of the agents, you know, rather than being just pulled into an IDE or just pulled into prototyping, but being able to still do the traditional design work at a faster pace. I think it's really, really important.
turns.zh: 我们看到现在创建的软件比以往任何时候都多，工程团队现在进展神速。我不知道你怎么看，但我并没有觉得软件在变得更好。过去 6 个月里，我还没有遇到过让我惊艳的软件体验。所以这对我们来说很重要，我从小就是软件的粉丝。我喜欢构建优秀的软件。你能给我的最好赞美就是 Paper 是一款真正优秀的软件。所以我希望世界上有更多这样的软件，我希望帮助设计师和有品味的人跟上所有正在创建的软件的步伐。所以，给他们一个能够以提示和智能体的速度运行的工具，而不是仅仅被拖入 IDE 或原型制作中，但仍然能够以更快的速度进行传统设计工作。我认为这真的非常重要。

turns.en: I'd love to see a demo. Can you show us how it works?
turns.zh: 我很想看一个演示。你能给我们展示一下它是如何工作的吗？

turns.en: Yeah, let's jump in. So it's a very familiar interface if you've used canvas tools. Sometimes I like to start with the visual things. So because we are using basically the browser to render, we can also render shaders really easily.
turns.zh: 好的，我们开始吧。如果你用过画布工具，这个界面会非常熟悉。有时候我喜欢从视觉元素开始。因为基本上我们是用浏览器来渲染，所以我们也能很容易地渲染着色器。

turns.en: And shaders are these basically WebGL animations that we build. This is called Paper Shaders. It's a library we put together. It's fully open source, fully, you know, feel free to use it for whatever you want to do. And the shaders are just so fun and brand designers love these because you can get all kinds of different looks. This is just one shader with different settings. And so you can do all kinds of stuff.
turns.zh: 着色器基本上就是我们构建的 WebGL 动画。这个叫 Paper Shaders，是我们整理的一个库。它完全开源，完全，你知道，随便你怎么用都行。而且着色器特别好玩，品牌设计师们很喜欢，因为你可以得到各种不同的视觉效果。这只是一个着色器配上不同的设置，所以你可以做各种花样。

turns.en: I know at YC, you guys have been using
turns.zh: 我知道在 YC，你们一直在用

turns.en: We've been using these all the time. We love it.
turns.zh: 我们一直在用这些，我们很喜欢。

turns.en: And I think, you know, for us and and I imagine a lot of people out there, this is probably their first introduction to using Paper. This is something that feels very modern, cutting edge, that would have been really difficult to do a year ago. And then you guys have made this really simple and native to the product to the point where it's showing up everywhere because it's so easy to do it now, right?
turns.zh: 而且我觉得，你知道，对我们来说，而且我想很多人，这可能是他们第一次接触使用 Paper。这感觉非常现代、前沿，一年前还很难做到。然后你们把这个做得非常简单，而且原生集成到产品里，以至于现在到处都在用，因为太容易了，对吧？

turns.en: That was part of our hope, was like can we make this more accessible to designers? Because if you're a designer and you're, you know, living in a traditional design tool all day, you want to create a shader effect. You want to describe how an AI loading state is working. And that's what I kept hearing, was I need to make loading states for AI and how do I do it? And so we just thought it'd be nice to give people these animated effects that they can customize and, you know, not just use the out of the box ones, but you can get in here and like tweak things and make them your own. And you can do all kinds of cool stuff. You can do blending modes, of course, to create combinations. Um, and you can also, these have been really popular, is some of these more subtle effects. This is a halftone dots. And you can pull other things into the effect. So this is pulling this, what we call neuro noise, into the halftone dots, and you can try different things and get different effects. Um, and we spent so much time. We actually studied literal paper to study the randomness of, you know, actual physical effects, and we try to model that in code. And so I think it's one of the reasons our shader library stands out, is we go to ridiculous degrees to make it as good as we possibly can. And so brand designers really love this. So like, you know, one example is Quarter. I don't know if you guys know the Quarter posters. Um, they are really, really cool posters that this team makes, that they do, I think it's like earning reports. And they've transitioned a lot of these to be built in Paper now, because they can get this cool retro, you know, vibe that, and really fast. So I love this. The work they're doing is really cool, and I'm like honored that they're using Paper to achieve some of these posters.
turns.zh: 那部分是我们的希望，就是能不能让设计师更容易上手？因为如果你是个设计师，整天泡在传统设计工具里，你想创建一个着色器效果，你想描述 AI 加载状态是怎么工作的。我一直听到的就是，我需要为 AI 做加载状态，我该怎么做？所以我们想，不如给大家这些可以定制的动画效果，你知道，不只是用现成的，你还可以进去调整，让它们变成你自己的。你可以做各种酷炫的东西。当然你可以用混合模式来创造组合。嗯，而且还有一些更微妙的特效也很受欢迎。这是半调网点。你可以把其他东西拉进效果里。所以这是把所谓的神经噪声拉进半调网点，你可以尝试不同的东西，得到不同的效果。嗯，我们花了大量时间。我们真的研究了真实的纸张，研究物理效果的随机性，然后尝试在代码里建模。所以我觉得我们的着色器库能脱颖而出，原因之一就是我们花了离谱的功夫让它尽可能好。品牌设计师真的很喜欢这个。比如，你知道，一个例子是 Quarter。不知道你们知不知道 Quarter 海报。嗯，那是这个团队做的非常酷的海报，他们做的是，我觉得是财报。他们现在把很多都改成用 Paper 做了，因为他们能快速得到那种复古的感觉。所以我喜欢这个。他们做的作品真的很酷，我很荣幸他们用 Paper 来实现这些海报。

turns.en: Yeah, it's really cool. We've used it for, we have Startup School, and so Ev, who leads design here at YC, has actually created custom animated shaders with the YC branding with people's names on them, tickets that are, you know, you can play with and animate when people get accepted and send it to them, and it's a great experience for the person receiving it. It feels very thoughtful and intentional and highly designed, and it's also creates something that's very shareable that people want to share out, which helps to spread the word also, all because of the design and because of the shaders.
turns.zh: 是的，真的很酷。我们在 Startup School 里用过，YC 的设计负责人 Ev 实际上做了定制的动画着色器，带有 YC 品牌标识和人名，做成门票，你知道，当人们被录取时，你可以玩一下、做动画，然后发给他们，对收到的人来说是很棒的体验。感觉非常贴心、用心、设计感十足，而且它也能创造出人们愿意分享的东西，这有助于传播，也都是因为设计和着色器。

turns.en: Really fast way to elevate the visuals and help it be a little more special.
turns.zh: 这是提升视觉效果、让它更特别一点的非常快的方法。

turns.en: So, shaders are very popular with the brand designers. We also do, this is kind of like a lesser known thing to Paper. We actually have a really great image generation library where you can use all kinds of models all at once. And so, I don't know, we'll just do a thoughtful man staring at the moon illustration. You can imagine for a brand piece or whatever you're working on. And so, this will use four different models at once, and you can quickly explore the possibility space of whatever kind of illustration you need to do.
turns.zh: 所以，着色器在品牌设计师中非常受欢迎。我们还有，这个对 Paper 来说可能不太为人所知。我们实际上有一个很棒图像生成库，你可以同时使用各种模型。所以，我不知道，我们就做一个沉思的男人凝视月亮的插画。你可以想象用在品牌物料或者你正在做的任何东西上。所以，这会同时使用四个不同的模型，你可以快速探索你需要的任何插画的可能性空间。

turns.en: That's very cool. Yeah, so I see you have it set to variety pack there. Is that the thing that gives you the four at once?
turns.zh: 那太酷了。是的，我看到你那里设置成了 variety pack。是那个让你一次得到四个的吗？

turns.en: You can pick a certain model if you want to. They all have different strengths and weaknesses, or you can do the variety pack and get, we kind of rotate which models are in there just as new models are always coming out, and it just lets you quickly explore. And you can provide inputs into it. You can, that's like, you know, I'll copy this shader as an image, and then you can feed the image into it and make this more colorful, please. So, you can do all kinds of different workflows combining these, you know, things to create really cool graphics really, really fast. Along the same lines, you can also vectorize. You can do this, extract colors is really, let's do this one. That's what I would try to do with this site is keep the excitement, keep this kind of like international... like that. It's unique. But you can't go so far, you know, maybe this text gradient is a little too wild and doesn't feel super trustworthy. But I do like the value prop, and I understand what it is for the most part pretty quickly, which I like.
turns.zh: 嗯，但我认为它给了你更多一点的基础……而且再说一次，你可以进来删除一些 vibe 编码的东西。少即是多。这就是我想对这个网站做的：保持兴奋感，保持这种国际化的感觉……就像那样。它很独特。但你不能走得太远，你知道，也许这个文字渐变有点太狂野了，感觉不太可信。但我确实喜欢这个价值主张，而且我大部分情况下很快就能理解它是做什么的，我喜欢这一点。

turns.en: I like that they've got a QR code in the bottom right.
turns.zh: 我喜欢他们右下角有个二维码。

turns.en: Which is part of the product, right? It's like...
turns.zh: 这是产品的一部分，对吧？就像……

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 对。

turns.en: Which is cool. That's something that I haven't seen very much before.
turns.zh: 这很酷。这是我以前不太常见到的东西。

turns.en: It makes me want to interact with it. It's inviting.
turns.zh: 它让我想和它互动。它很有吸引力。

turns.en: Yep.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: Yep. The overall feeling, the vibe is... If we can make it a little more trustworthy, but I like the excitement, I like the energy, I like the invitation that I have.
turns.zh: 是的。整体感觉，那种氛围是……如果我们能让它更可信一点，但我喜欢这种兴奋感，我喜欢这种能量，我喜欢它给我的邀请感。

turns.en: Yeah, it's almost too easy to miss it down in that corner, though, too, cuz, you know, you're so used to seeing the chat with us box down, and you just assume there's a bunch of things that you should ignore.
turns.zh: 对，不过它也几乎太容易让人忽略在角落里了，因为你知道，你太习惯看到右下角的聊天框了，你会假设有一堆东西应该忽略。

turns.en: That are unless you have a problem, like that's where you look. And I don't know, maybe they should bring that QR code up to the main area and say, "Try it now."
turns.zh: 那些东西除非你有问题，否则你不会看。我不知道，也许他们应该把二维码放到主区域，说“现在试试”。

turns.en: Spit in the hero.
turns.zh: 放在主视觉里。

turns.en: Yeah. Yeah.
turns.zh: 对，对。

turns.en: I do feel like this hero could be working a lot harder for that. Cuz when I start getting down here, I'm like, "Yeah, this is good. This is solid." It seems to get more trustworthy the further you go.
turns.zh: 我确实觉得这个主视觉可以更努力地发挥作用。因为当我往下看的时候，我会想：“对，这不错。这很扎实。”越往下越显得可信。

turns.en: Mhm. Yeah, it is interesting your point that, you know, at the end of the day the models are the ones that are generating the design when you use them to generate the design. And you're kind of at the mercy for how like what they've been trained on and how they like to design.
turns.zh: 嗯。对，你说的这点很有意思，你知道，归根结底，当你用模型生成设计时，是模型在生成设计。你有点受制于它们被训练了什么、它们喜欢怎么设计。

turns.en: Yes, yeah.
turns.zh: 是的，对。

turns.en: And so what's important is using the right models and those models getting better at design, which will inevitably happen over time. And then the next thing that you need is just more control over it quickly.
turns.zh: 所以重要的是使用正确的模型，而这些模型会随着时间推移不可避免地变得更好。然后你需要的下一件事就是更快地获得更多控制权。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 对。

turns.en: And so to have that control, to be able to edit it and make it more in your own vision, is actually the really powerful missing piece here that I think is a lot of what Paper is providing right here.
turns.zh: 所以拥有这种控制权，能够编辑它并让它更符合你自己的愿景，实际上是这里真正缺失的强大部分，我认为这正是 Paper 在这里提供的很多东西。

turns.en: The agents can speed you up. They can save you a lot of work, and they can do tasks like translation or resizing for you. But we're big believers in the human element of design and how important that is. And so we're trying to create a tool that lets humans work really fast with agents.
turns.zh: 智能体可以加速你的工作。它们可以帮你省很多事，还能帮你做翻译或调整尺寸之类的任务。但我们坚信设计中人的因素及其重要性。所以我们试图创造一个工具，让人类能和智能体一起非常快速地工作。

turns.en: Do you think the agents can learn taste the same way humans can?
turns.zh: 你觉得智能体能不能像人类一样学会品味？

turns.en: They'll get better at things like letter spacing, the little tactical things will get better over time. And I think what I'm encouraged by is a model like Fable seems much more thoughtful. It feels like it actually put some choice, some thought into its decisions compared to previous models. And so I think that is a piece of design, is that thoughtfulness.
turns.zh: 它们会在字距之类的事情上变得更好，那些小的战术性事情会随着时间推移变得更好。而且我觉得让我受到鼓舞的是，像 Fable 这样的模型似乎更有思想。感觉它实际上比以前的模型在决策中投入了更多选择和思考。所以我认为这就是设计的一部分，就是那种深思熟虑。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 对。

turns.en: Now, do I ever think it's going to replace a human making these design decisions? No, no way. Because a lot of design is actually a very human task of like decision-making in an organization. It's showing people comps and being... and people can be like, "Oh, not like that. I don't like that." The role of design is... you see the pixels at the end, but the role of design in an org is like decisions and stakeholders and bringing in requirements and problem space, and those are not things that agents have any skill at really. You know, who knows over time. They're going to get smarter and smarter and smarter, but I just think humans are such an essential piece of building stuff that stands out from the crowd.
turns.zh: 那么，我是否认为它会取代人类做这些设计决策？不，绝不可能。因为很多设计实际上是组织中非常人性化的决策任务。它向人们展示方案，然后人们可能会说：“哦，不是那样。我不喜欢那样。”设计的角色是……你最后看到的是像素，但设计在组织中的角色是决策、利益相关者、引入需求和问题空间，这些都不是智能体真正擅长的。你知道，谁知道随着时间的推移会怎样。它们会变得越来越聪明，但我就是认为人类是构建脱颖而出之物的关键部分。

turns.en: Yeah, it's interesting. I was having a very similar conversation with someone who leads design at a multi-billion dollar design-forward company about there's a thought process that goes through a human's head where they're reacting to something and a criteria they're evaluating and it's very implicit for us as humans right now. And the question is can you verbalize what those things are?
turns.zh: 对，这很有意思。我和一位在数十亿美元、以设计为先的公司领导设计的人有过非常相似的对话，关于人类脑海中有一个思考过程，他们在对某件事做出反应，并有一个评估标准，这对我们人类来说目前是非常隐性的。问题是，你能把这些东西说出来吗？

turns.en: Mhm.
turns.zh: 嗯。

turns.en: Like what is the process of you deciding whether something is good or not or looks good or not or hits the bar or not. Can you literally go through and quantify all of that and teach that to a model to the point where it has taste like a human would? And then the question becomes well if all the models were able to do that, does everything just look the same again?
turns.zh: 比如你决定某件事好不好、看起来好不好、是否达到标准的这个过程是什么。你能真正地逐一量化所有这些，并教给模型，让它拥有像人类一样的品味吗？然后问题就变成了，如果所有模型都能做到这一点，是不是一切又会看起来一样了？

turns.en: And then you always need the humans to be driving to finding the next thing that's actually going to be new and stands out and pushes the limits more.
turns.zh: 然后你总是需要人类去推动寻找下一个真正新颖、脱颖而出、更能突破极限的东西。

turns.en: We see that even within human pre-pre-models as trends take over. You know, everyone kind of looks like linear for a couple years and then somebody else figures out something, right? I do think the models will get good at tactics. They'll get better at not making everything bold. You know, and I think that that's great and that'll be really nice. But the just the thought, the product, there's so much of design again, it's like was this showing value prop or not? That stuff's more important. This site for instance that I think is a little too wild, maybe it's really important for them to be really fun and exciting. Maybe that's what their market needs.
turns.zh: 我们看到即使在人类的前模型时代，趋势也会接管。你知道，每个人都看起来像线性风格几年，然后别人发现了新东西，对吧？我确实认为模型会在战术上变得擅长。它们会更好地避免把所有东西都加粗。你知道，我认为那很棒，那会非常好。但仅仅是想法、产品，设计中有太多东西，就像它是否展示了价值主张？那些东西更重要。比如这个网站，我觉得有点太狂野了，也许对他们来说，真正有趣和令人兴奋非常重要。也许这就是他们的市场需要的。

turns.en: Mhm.
turns.zh: 嗯。

turns.en: You know, and so maybe it's a higher order thing for them to be very exciting and kind of model decision can... you know, maybe with enough information you could start to get there, but I think we're pretty far away from that. Yeah, maybe 10 years something like that. Maybe I don't know, maybe I'm too pessimistic. Maybe it'll come sooner. But I still see humans as just this essential piece of the puzzle.
turns.zh: 你知道，所以也许对他们来说，保持非常兴奋和某种模型决策是更高层次的事情……你知道，也许有足够的信息你就能开始接近，但我认为我们离那还很远。对，也许 10 年左右。也许我不知道，也许我太悲观了。也许它会来得更早。但我仍然认为人类是拼图中不可或缺的一部分。

turns.en: Yeah, we certainly hope so.
turns.zh: 对，我们当然希望如此。

turns.en: Yeah, let's hope so.
turns.zh: 对，希望如此。

turns.en: I'm curious how are you guys using agents internally at Paper?
turns.zh: 我很好奇你们在 Paper 内部是怎么使用智能体的？

turns.en: In some ways we use them a lot and then in other ways we use them... we're kind of like dinosaurs in some ways.
turns.zh: 在某些方面我们用得很多，但在其他方面我们用得……我们在某些方面有点像恐龙。

turns.en: Like, we don't have agents in our Slack, and we don't... we use agents for coding quite a bit, but we still read our code. We read all of our code, every single line.
turns.zh: 比如，我们的 Slack 里没有智能体，我们也不会……我们在编码时确实大量使用智能体，但我们仍然会阅读代码。我们阅读所有代码，每一行。

turns.en: Every line.
turns.zh: 每一行。

turns.en: Usually multiple humans read every single line.
turns.zh: 通常会有多个人类阅读每一行。

turns.en: Why is that?
turns.zh: 为什么？

turns.en: Well, one is design tools are really hard to build. You know, you can't write a code design tool at the level of a Figma today. Maybe you can eventually. And so it takes a lot of really precise, really careful work. It's very multi-dimensional in terms of the systems. And so we just have to be really careful. And we want to make sure our experience, you know, designers need 120 FPS. It needs to be fast. It needs to work every single time. And the agents just aren't there.
turns.zh: 嗯，一是设计工具真的很难构建。你知道，今天你无法写出 Figma 级别的代码设计工具。也许最终可以。所以这需要大量非常精确、非常细致的工作。从系统角度来看，它是非常多维的。所以我们必须要非常小心。我们希望确保我们的体验，你知道，设计师需要 120 FPS。它必须快。它必须每次都正常工作。而智能体还达不到。

turns.en: Not yet.
turns.zh: 还没有。

turns.en: The other thing is a small elite team, right? So 12 people keep the talent bar extremely high. I think when you're building companies, that's how you should try to do it these days. And use the agents to accelerate the people. But if you have less people, you have less communication burden, you have less of these other costs to go through.
turns.zh: 另一件事是精英小团队，对吧？所以 12 个人保持极高的人才标准。我认为如今在创办公司时，你应该尝试这样做。并用智能体来加速人员。但如果人更少，沟通负担更少，其他成本也更少。

turns.en: One example of how we use agents though is Agu, our brand designer. He's a brilliant brand designer, great at visuals. He codes a little bit, but I don't think he'd call himself a programmer. And he made our entire website in about a week before this last launch.
turns.zh: 不过，我们使用智能体的一个例子是我们的品牌设计师 Agu。他是一位出色的品牌设计师，擅长视觉。他会一点编码，但我觉得他不会称自己为程序员。他在上次发布前大约一周内完成了我们整个网站。

turns.en: Wow.
turns.zh: 哇。

turns.en: Including shipping it, including all of the animations. And he designed everything in Paper. And this is the kind of design you wouldn't want to do this with prompting, right? You need this... he has shaders in the background subtly coming through these motifs. He did everything in Paper, and then he just prompted. And this was, you know, 6 months ago now, so different models. He just prompted the animations on top of his Paper file. He was like, you know, take my Paper designs, turn it into a code base. This is a Next.js site, and put it together for me. No one else looked at this. So Agu did this end-to-end in a week. Because he's a designer, he puts in these Easter eggs. There's little like fun extras.
turns.zh: 包括发布，包括所有动画。他在 Paper 中设计了所有内容。而这种设计你不想用提示词来做，对吧？你需要这个……他在背景中有着色器，微妙地贯穿这些主题。他在 Paper 中做了所有事情，然后他只是提示。而这是，你知道，6 个月前了，所以是不同的模型。他只是在 Paper 文件之上提示动画。他说，你知道，把我的 Paper 设计变成一个代码库。这是一个 Next.js 网站，帮我整合起来。没有其他人看过这个。所以 Agu 在一周内端到端完成了。因为他是个设计师，他加入了这些彩蛋。有一些有趣的小额外内容。

turns.en: And it's all just interactive.
turns.zh: 而且它完全是交互式的。

turns.en: It's interactive. And this is something he would not have done. He wouldn't have had the time. I'm sure he could have, you know, skill-wise he could have got there, but like he wouldn't have the time to do this. So I think that's really, really cool. And so I think a lot of times it shows up more not in our core product, where we're actually pretty human-based still for precision reasons. But in all the other stuff, all the videos we need to make, all the marketing site, all of that other stuff where we can, you know, have agents help us help people go faster.
turns.zh: 它是交互式的。而这是他本来不会做的事情。他不会有时间。我相信他本可以，你知道，从技能上讲他本可以达到，但他不会有时间做这个。所以我认为这真的非常酷。所以我认为很多时候它更多出现在我们的核心产品之外，在核心产品中我们实际上仍然非常依赖人工，出于精确性的原因。但在所有其他方面，所有我们需要制作的视频，所有营销网站，所有那些我们可以让智能体帮助人们更快完成的事情。

turns.en: Yep. So we do, yeah, quite a bit of that and then of course the coding agents, you know, we do use Cursor extensively, we use Claude Code extensively, we use Bug Bot for our PR reviews, which has been really helpful. It's a little too pedantic sometimes, but it still catches bugs, which is good.
turns.zh: 是的。所以我们确实，嗯，做了不少，然后当然还有编码智能体，你知道，我们广泛使用 Cursor，我们广泛使用 Claude Code，我们使用 Bug Bot 进行 PR 审查，这非常有帮助。它有时有点过于迂腐，但它仍然能捕获错误，这很好。

turns.en: There's a little bit of a FOMO right now with agents. So it's like, oh every company is shipping without looking at their code. Are you going too slow, you know? We are kind of taking the approach that quality software takes time.
turns.zh: 现在对智能体有一点 FOMO。所以就像，哦，每家公司都在不查看代码的情况下发布。你是不是太慢了，你知道？我们有点采取质量软件需要时间的做法。

turns.en: Mhm.
turns.zh: 嗯。

turns.en: And we have competitors that have every single feature. But they don't have the attention or people don't care. And for whatever reason, whatever that is, it's like people want Paper to be better. They don't want the competitors that have every single feature to be better. And I think that's because we care and we're putting in that precision and that care about these things. So even if we're moving a little slower, people still care more about it and so I think that quality matters. So thankfully.
turns.zh: 而且我们有竞争对手拥有每一个功能。但他们没有关注度，或者人们不在乎。不管出于什么原因，就像人们希望 Paper 更好。他们不希望拥有每一个功能的竞争对手更好。我认为那是因为我们在乎，我们投入了那种精确性和关怀。所以即使我们移动得慢一点，人们仍然更在乎它，所以我认为质量很重要。所以谢天谢地。

turns.en: My sense from talking to a lot of designers is that you guys are almost building kind of a groundswell movement. Like a cult movement of people that are now using Paper as the new cool thing that a lot of designers are using and it's the new modern way to work. Was that intentional and what are the things that you're doing to try to get more users, to grow, to get some mind share? Like you seem to be one of the only companies... Figma obviously has built this huge behemoth and gone public and you know, all the Fortune 500 uses them and all this stuff, but it feels like you've started to crack some of that. Certainly within certain user types. And how have you gone about doing that and what's been most successful for you there?
turns.zh: 我与很多设计师交谈后感觉，你们几乎在建立一种草根运动。就像一种小众运动，人们现在使用 Paper 作为新的酷东西，很多设计师都在使用，这是新的现代工作方式。这是有意的吗？你们在做什么来获得更多用户、增长、获得一些心智份额？比如你们似乎是唯一一家……Figma 显然已经建立了这个巨大的庞然大物并上市了，你知道，财富 500 强都用它，所有这些，但感觉你们已经开始撬动一些了。当然在某些用户类型中。你们是怎么做到的？对你们来说什么最成功？

turns.en: Yeah, a huge part of that is being very values aligned with the market. We didn't have a product for the first year and we still got to about 25,000 Twitter followers just by talking about our values. You know, just go on podcast be like I really like design. Do you like design? We then get into the topic and talk about typography or whatever. Being values aligned with your market, they will forgive so much about your product missing things. They'll wait for them to come out. They'll root for you if they can tell you're authentic. You know, and if you're building design software, it really matters. It really matters. Maybe not for all software, but for design software, usually best product, most authentic product wins. And so I think for us it was just, you know, again, company of 12 designers and engineers and just live our values and people really resonate with that. And by the way, the product is really good, too. I think that that part's important. You got to get there. But, you know, I think that's part of it. And then there's market clock. Every company... Hopefully we have this problem someday. Every company eventually goes up market and you just stop being as cool when you do that, you know? You're selling to enterprises. You're not underground at the cool events, you know, anymore. So, I'm really honored that we are part of the community. And to your point, like I think you saw, you know, Ramp has been releasing the data of actual Ramp subscriptions on their credit cards. Yeah. And if they released an AI you can chat with about the Ramp data. And if you ask it about design tools, it's, you know, Figma obviously. Sketch is there. And then Paper is right there with Sketch. And so we're the first company since Figma's come out to like make a dent in that market at all, you know? And it's growing very quickly. Which is really encouraging. It's really exciting cuz you don't know when you start a company like how it's going to go. You have no idea. Like I said, there were months where I was like nobody's going to care about this.
turns.zh: 是的，很大一部分是与市场价值观高度一致。第一年我们没有产品，但仅通过谈论我们的价值观就获得了大约 25,000 名 Twitter 粉丝。你知道，只是上播客说我真的喜欢设计。你喜欢设计吗？然后我们进入话题，谈论排版或其他什么。与市场价值观一致，他们会原谅你产品缺失很多东西。他们会等待它们出现。如果他们能看出你是真诚的，他们会为你加油。你知道，如果你在构建设计软件，这真的很重要。真的很重要。也许不是对所有软件，但对于设计软件，通常最好的产品、最真诚的产品会赢。所以我认为对我们来说，你知道，再次，12 人的设计师和工程师公司，只是践行我们的价值观，人们真的能产生共鸣。顺便说一句，产品也非常好。我认为那部分很重要。你必须达到。但是，你知道，我认为这是其中的一部分。然后是市场时机。每家公司……希望我们有一天也有这个问题。每家公司最终都会向上市场移动，当你这样做时，你就不再那么酷了，你知道？你向企业销售。你不再在地下酷活动中了，你知道。所以，我真的很荣幸能成为社区的一部分。至于你的观点，比如我想你看到了，你知道，Ramp 一直在发布他们信用卡上实际 Ramp 订阅的数据。是的。如果他们发布了一个你可以与之聊天的关于 Ramp 数据的 AI。如果你问它关于设计工具的问题，它，你知道，显然是 Figma。Sketch 也在那里。然后 Paper 就在 Sketch 旁边。所以我们是自 Figma 出现以来第一家在那个市场有所作为的公司，你知道？而且它增长非常快。这真的很鼓舞人心。真的很令人兴奋，因为当你创办一家公司时，你不知道它会如何发展。你完全不知道。就像我说的，有几个月我都在想没人会在乎这个。

turns.en: And to now have like so many cool people, um people are way cooler than me, that care a lot about Paper and are like wearing our merch and stuff is like so much fun to see.
turns.zh: 而现在有这么多酷的人，嗯，比我酷得多的人，非常关心 Paper，并且穿着我们的周边商品等等，看到这些真是太有趣了。

turns.en: And honestly, it's the best part.
turns.zh: 老实说，这是最棒的部分。

turns.en: That's really cool. And this is not your first company. This is your second company, right? And it seems like even before you had a product, you have gotten yourself out there and your vision and your values and you become the ambassador and that's what people were buying into before you had a product and certainly in the early days of having a product and that's what's been successful is you. And getting that out there. And how is that different from you, you know, you built another company before this and like contrast the two?
turns.zh: 这太酷了。而且这不是你的第一家公司，这是你的第二家公司，对吧？看起来甚至在你有产品之前，你就已经把自己、你的愿景和价值观展现出来了，你成为了代言人，这就是人们在你有产品之前，以及产品早期所认同的东西，而成功的正是你本人，以及你把这些传播出去。那么，这和你之前创办的另一家公司有什么不同？对比一下这两者？

turns.en: Well, so my first company Modules was working on design and developer handoff.
turns.zh: 嗯，我的第一家公司 Modules 做的是设计和开发交接。

turns.en: Mhm.
turns.zh: 嗯。

turns.en: And we built Radix UI along the way. It was like one of our side projects that just kept going. And, you know, Radix became this default React component library.
turns.zh: 我们在这个过程中还做了 Radix UI。它就像是我们一个一直持续下去的副项目。然后，你知道，Radix 成了默认的 React 组件库。

turns.en: Mhm.
turns.zh: 嗯。

turns.en: One was this was pre-AI. So, you know, everything was harder. Designer-developer handoff was harder. Two was we really listened to both sides at once and we got very confused. Because designers want engineers to change and engineers want designers to change and like they will tell you the other team will use your software. Like you can't build software that way. And so we learned some hard lessons about making something people actually want. And then I think I've been able to apply that at Paper. But, we did make, I mean the Radix has amazing product market fit. We just didn't see a way to build like a venture scale business around it. And so we thought let's just make it free and give it away and then, you know, come back with something next time. And so that's been cool. I mean that worked out really well. We sold this company to WorkOS, which is an amazing auth and identity company. We use WorkOS for Paper. And then a couple years after that I just wanted to start back into creative tooling again.
turns.zh: 第一，这是 AI 之前的事。所以，你知道，一切都更难。设计和开发交接更难。第二，我们真的同时听取双方的意见，结果我们很困惑。因为设计师希望工程师改变，工程师希望设计师改变，而且他们会告诉你对方团队会使用你的软件。你不能那样构建软件。所以我们学到了一些关于做出人们真正想要的东西的惨痛教训。然后我想我已经能够把这些应用到 Paper 上。但是，我们确实做出了，我的意思是 Radix 有惊人的产品市场契合度。我们只是没看到围绕它建立风险投资规模业务的方法。所以我们想，那就让它免费，把它送出去，然后，你知道，下次再带着新东西回来。所以这很酷。我的意思是那结果非常好。我们把这公司卖给了 WorkOS，一家很棒的认证和身份公司。我们在 Paper 上使用 WorkOS。然后几年后，我又想重新开始做创意工具。

turns.en: And are there any lessons that you took from that experience that you're applying this time?
turns.zh: 那你从那次经历中学到了什么教训，这次在应用吗？

turns.en: You can way overcomplicate product building. You know, the make something people want is a great phrase. And you really a lot of times when you with your product it's like what does my company need next? What would be like the best thing that possibly could happen to my company right now? At the beginning for us that was like being part of the conversation, having Twitter followers. Well, let's go do things that get Twitter followers. Let's go on a podcast. Let's talk to users and then represent their values outwardly. So, you know, a lot of times it's actually very simple. And I think we make it too complicated and we're trying to have these brilliant strategies for our companies and it's like what do you need next and just do the most straightforward thing you can possibly do to get there. And you know, and don't be scared to do things that sound hard, you know, obviously you got to do them. So, that's the philosophy we've taken a bottleneck first huge huge philosophy I really believe in. Like for us right now the bottleneck is early adopters are using Paper. The people that are more, you know, maybe not an early adopter type are very used to what they're doing now. And they're missing features like comments and components. And so now our bottleneck is actually features again. And so now it's like well that's what we got to go do next. And release that bottleneck to the business. Another just like a tactical thing is just like talking to users every day. So so important. I had a rule the first year of the company I had to talk to a designer every single day and I did it all the way through the year. And that was so useful cuz I learned just how like when you start making the company and the product you just have a different perspective. You can't help it. You have personal knowledge. And so just staying rooted in user conversations is really important.
turns.zh: 你可能会把产品构建过度复杂化。你知道，“做出人们想要的东西”是个好说法。很多时候，当你面对产品时，你会想：我的公司下一步需要什么？现在可能发生在我公司身上的最好的事情是什么？对我们来说，一开始就是成为对话的一部分，拥有 Twitter 粉丝。好吧，那就去做能涨粉的事情。去上播客。去和用户交谈，然后向外传达他们的价值观。所以，你知道，很多时候其实很简单。我认为我们把它搞得太复杂了，我们试图为公司制定那些绝妙的战略，但其实就是要弄清楚下一步需要什么，然后尽可能用最直接的方式去实现。而且，不要害怕做那些听起来很难的事情，显然你必须去做。所以，这就是我们采取的理念，瓶颈优先，我非常相信这个理念。比如我们现在，瓶颈是早期采用者在使用 Paper。那些可能不是早期采用者类型的人，非常习惯他们现在的工作方式。他们缺少评论和组件等功能。所以现在我们的瓶颈又变成了功能。所以现在，那就是我们下一步要做的。把那个瓶颈释放给业务。另一个战术上的事情就是每天和用户交谈。非常重要。我在公司第一年有个规矩，我必须每天和一个设计师交谈，我坚持了一整年。那非常有用，因为我了解到，当你开始创建公司和产品时，你会有不同的视角。你忍不住，你有个人知识。所以保持扎根于用户对话非常重要。

turns.en: Yeah, it gets harder and harder to do that as the company grows and scales also because there's so many other things that are vying for your time and pulling you in different directions and that seem important or here on fire in the moment. Yeah. But really it's those core fundamental things of build your product, talk to users, and you know, exercise or whatever you need to do so you don't go crazy doing the first two things. But that's the core of it for the life of the company, right? And that's it. And so it's cool to hear that you've done that from the very first day and I'm sure it is something that has been instilled culturally in your team now and that everybody is talking to users at this point.
turns.zh: 是的，随着公司成长和扩张，这变得越来越难，因为有很多其他事情在争夺你的时间，把你拉向不同的方向，那些事情看起来很重要，或者当下很紧急。是的。但真正核心的是那些基本的东西：构建产品、和用户交谈，还有，你知道，锻炼或者任何你需要做的事情，这样你就不会因为做前两件事而发疯。但这就是公司的核心，对吧？就是这样。所以很高兴听到你从第一天就这么做了，我相信这已经在你的团队文化中根深蒂固了，现在每个人都在和用户交谈。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: and that everybody is talking to users at this point.
turns.zh: 而且现在每个人都在和用户交谈。

turns.en: Oh yeah. Yeah, that's when people onboard it's like you yeah, you have to be in the Discord talking to people or in the Slack. It's really really important. And not everyone's comfortable. Maybe they've come from a bigger company where they were told they can't talk to users and you know, it's like no, get in there. You can't screw it up. And you just learn so much. And I think it guides your decision-making. Your decisions are really important in a company. You can kind of look at like successful companies of like you can trace their decisions backwards in time of like oh, that was an inflection point. That decision was really good. And so I think having an informed employee base. Like I can't make every decision in the company. Even at 12 people there's no way I could do that. And so if you can have your employees be really informed about users and what they actually want, you'll have good decisions being made all over, you know, all over the place. And I yeah, it's really important.
turns.zh: 哦，是的。是的，当人们入职时，就像，你必须进入 Discord 和人们交谈，或者在 Slack 里。这真的非常重要。而且不是每个人都舒服。也许他们来自大公司，被告知不能和用户交谈，你知道，但事实是，不，进去吧。你不会搞砸的。你只是学到很多。我认为它指导你的决策。决策在公司里非常重要。你可以看看成功的公司，你可以追溯他们的决策，比如，哦，那是一个转折点。那个决策非常好。所以我认为拥有一个信息灵通的员工基础。比如我不能做公司里的每一个决策。即使只有 12 个人，我也不可能做到。所以如果你能让你的员工真正了解用户以及他们真正想要什么，你就会在各地做出好的决策，你知道，到处都是。而且，是的，这非常重要。

turns.en: What do you think is next for design?
turns.zh: 你认为设计的下一步是什么？

turns.en: Well, I think a lot of design isn't changing. Again, in orgs it's like the function of design is still really important as a way to explore problem space, competitive analysis, executive stakeholders, things like this. We're not seeing that change at all. And so, you know, that function of design I think is sticking around. If anything, I think we're going to see more because there are more companies and there's more software to be made. So, we're seeing just more and more design need in the world. I do think the tooling is going to accelerate because I think we just need to be able to keep the quality bar up at a pace that is, you know, keeping up with the engineering, with the product teams. The software will ship whether the designer gets a chance to make it better or not. It's just kind of like a reality of the competitive landscape. So, how do we help make sure that the designer can be part of the conversation and keep up in that shipping process.
turns.zh: 嗯，我认为很多设计并没有改变。再说一次，在组织中，设计的功能仍然非常重要，作为探索问题空间、竞争分析、高管利益相关者等等的方式。我们完全没有看到那方面的改变。所以，你知道，我认为设计的功能会保留。如果有的话，我认为我们会看到更多，因为有更多的公司，有更多的软件要制作。所以，我们看到世界上对设计的需求越来越多。我确实认为工具会加速发展，因为我认为我们需要能够以跟上工程和产品团队的速度保持质量水平。软件会发布，不管设计师有没有机会让它变得更好。这有点像竞争格局的现实。那么，我们如何帮助确保设计师能成为对话的一部分，并在发布过程中跟上节奏呢？

turns.en: But, you know, I think in general, sometimes I think there's less change coming than people think, actually, because I think that a lot of design is a very human problem, and the pixels at the end are like the output of the process, you know.
turns.zh: 但你知道，我觉得总的来说，有时候我认为变化并没有人们想象的那么大，因为我觉得很多设计是一个非常人性化的问题，最终的像素只是过程的输出，你懂的。

turns.en: It's the medium at the end of the day, right?
turns.zh: 说到底，它只是媒介，对吧？

turns.en: Exactly. Yeah. Yeah.
turns.zh: 没错。是的。是的。

turns.en: And what's next for Paper?
turns.zh: 那 Paper 接下来有什么计划？

turns.en: Well, so we are, like I said, we're building out some table stakes components, comments, bottleneck reducers. I'm really excited. Something I've learned from talking to users is people are building all these prototypes all over the place, and they're ending up on Vercel or their HTML files, and people don't know how to leave feedback on them, or how to even find which one someone's talking about. So, what we're going to do is we're going to put basically you can iframe things onto the Paper canvas as a place to keep your prototypes kind of organized, and then people can leave comments as they're used to doing on the prototypes. So, when people ask us if we're doing prototyping, it's like, well, kind of. We're going to help you organize your prototypes and have feedback cycles. And I think this is going to be a really big unlock for companies that are, you know, building playgrounds for the designers to vibe code in, but then it's kind of like this messy result and they need some tool to help them organize that. So, that's a big thing we're going to be working on the next, you know, 6 months or so as we're building out the table stakes that people expect.
turns.zh: 嗯，我们正在，就像我说的，我们在构建一些基础组件、评论、瓶颈消除器。我真的很兴奋。从与用户的交流中我学到的是，人们到处都在构建各种原型，它们最终放在 Vercel 上或作为 HTML 文件，而人们不知道如何在这些原型上留下反馈，甚至不知道如何找到别人在谈论的那个原型。所以，我们要做的是，基本上你可以把东西 iframe 到 Paper 画布上，作为一个整理原型的地方，然后人们可以像他们习惯的那样在原型上留下评论。所以，当人们问我们是否在做原型设计时，就像，嗯，算是吧。我们将帮助你组织你的原型，并建立反馈循环。我认为这对那些为设计师构建“氛围编码”游乐场的公司来说是一个巨大的解锁，但结果往往很混乱，他们需要一些工具来帮助组织。所以，这是我们在接下来的 6 个月左右要重点做的事情，因为我们正在构建人们期望的基础功能。

turns.en: Amazing. Steven, thank you so much for coming on and sharing Paper with us and all of your design insight that I know has been hard-earned over the years and the companies that you've built and the incredible places you've worked. So, thank you.
turns.zh: 太棒了。Steven，非常感谢你来做客，和我们分享 Paper，以及你所有的设计见解，我知道这些年来你在你建立的公司和你工作过的那些不可思议的地方，这些见解来之不易。所以，谢谢你。

turns.en: Yeah, thank you so much for having me.
turns.zh: 是的，非常感谢你的邀请。

turns.en: That does it for this episode of Design Review, and we'll see you on the next one.
turns.zh: 本期《设计评论》就到这里，我们下期再见。

tldr.en: Design is a key differentiator; great companies of the last 10-20 years all have exceptional design.
tldr.zh: 设计是关键差异化因素；过去 10-20 年的伟大公司都拥有卓越的设计。

tldr.en: Using HTML and CSS as the rendering engine makes it easier for agents to work with design tools.
tldr.zh: 使用 HTML 和 CSS 作为渲染引擎，使代理更容易与设计工具协作。

tldr.en: The codebase should be the single source of truth for design and development, eliminating the need for separate design systems.
tldr.zh: 代码库应成为设计和开发的唯一真实来源，无需单独的设计系统。
